sentiment.rationale: The company delivered strong Q1 results (34% revenue growth, $101B GMV) and provided Q2 guidance for high-20s revenue growth and mid-teens free cash flow margins, which represents a continuation of strong momentum rather than a formal raise above prior guidance. The document shows genuine operational inflection with broad-based growth across geographies, merchant sizes, and channels, plus accelerating AI adoption metrics (Sidekick weekly active shops up 385%, AI-driven orders up nearly 13x), supporting a positive but not strongly positive score. Forward guidance was held at a high level (high-20s revenue growth, mid-teens FCF margin) with confident management language, but no explicit raise above prior guidance was stated, and the company noted FX tailwinds of ~2 points in Q1 that will diminish to ~0.5 point in Q2, which tempers the score.

summary.revenue: $3.2 billion for Q1 2026, up 34% year-over-year (32% on a constant currency basis).
summary.guidance: Q2 2026: revenue growth expected in the high-twenties percentage rate year-over-year; gross profit dollars to grow at a mid-twenties percentage rate; operating expenses as a percentage of revenue to be 35% to 36%; stock-based compensation to be $145 million; free cash flow margin to be in the mid-teens.
summary.margin: Q1 2026 free cash flow margin was 15% of revenue. Gross profit grew 32% year-over-year. Operating expenses were 37% of revenue, a 4-point improvement from Q1 last year. Subscription Solutions gross margin was 80%, in line with Q1 2025. Merchant Solutions gross margin was 39%, essentially flat year-over-year.
key_risks: Transaction and loan losses came in at 3.7% of revenue, up from 3.2% in Q1 2025, with credit losses primarily responsible for the increase.
Increased LLM costs driven by growing merchant usage of AI products, most notably Sidekick, partially offset economies of scale and efficiencies in support.
Q2 revenue guidance assumes approximately 0.5 point of FX tailwinds versus the more than 2 points of FX tailwinds seen in Q1.

Forward-looking statements note risks including changes in economic conditions and consumer spending, tariffs, adoption of emerging technologies like AI, reliance on third-party providers, cyberattacks, and software defects.
key_opportunities: International GMV growth of 45% with cross-border GMV representing 16% of total; European GMV up 48% (35% constant currency).
B2B GMV grew 80% in Q1 with broad growth across new and established merchants.
Offline GMV rose 33%, with merchants operating more than 20 stores growing 50% year-over-year.
AI-driven traffic to Shopify stores grew 8x year-over-year, and orders from AI-powered searches increased nearly 13x.
Shopify Payments processed $67 billion of GMV, up 41%, reaching 67% penetration.
Shop Pay GMV processed $35 billion, up 59%, with international Shop Pay GMV growing over 70%.
Enterprise growth: merchants doing over $100 million in annual GMV have nearly doubled in two years.
Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) co-developed with Google, with Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, and Stripe joining the council.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management used highly confident language throughout, with Harley Finkelstein stating 'This is Shopify at its best' and describing the company as being in 'a category of one' with a 'compounding advantage.'
